title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 381 (Accounts of foreign company)

content.overview: Every foreign company shall, in every calendar year, make out a balance sheet and profit and loss account in such form, containing such particulars and including or having annexed or attached thereto such documents as may be prescribed, and deliver a copy of those documents to the Registrar. The Central Government may, by notification, direct that clause (a) shall not apply, or shall apply subject to exceptions and modifications, to any foreign company or class of foreign companies. If any such document is not in English, a certified English translation shall be annexed. Every foreign company shall also send to the Registrar, along with those documents, a copy of a list in the prescribed form of all places of business established by the company in India as at the date with reference to which the balance sheet is made out.
content.glance: Annual balance sheet and P&L in prescribed form, filed with the Registrar; English translation if needed; list of Indian places of business; Central Government may notify exceptions.
content.study: Section 381 imposes annual accounts and filing duties on foreign companies. The company must prepare a balance sheet and profit and loss account in the prescribed form and deliver them to the Registrar each calendar year, with a certified English translation where needed, and a list of all places of business in India as at the balance-sheet date. The Central Government may notify that the form-and-particulars requirement does not apply, or applies with modifications, to specified foreign companies or classes.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Every foreign company must annually prepare and file with the Registrar a balance sheet and P&L in prescribed form, with English translation if needed, and a list of Indian places of business; CG may notify exceptions.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 381
examples.body: A foreign company with branches in Delhi and Chennai files its annual balance sheet and P&L with the Registrar together with a list of those places of business under s. 381(3).

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 381?
hypotheticals.analysis: It requires annual accounts filing by foreign companies, with a list of Indian places of business, subject to possible Central Government exceptions.

rows.right: Documents on establishment (s. 380) or display of name (s. 382)

misconceptions.trap: Assuming Indian accounts duties under s. 128–129 automatically replace s. 381.
misconceptions.correction: s. 381 is the specific accounts-and-filing rule for foreign companies; general company accounts provisions apply only as Chapter XXII directs.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 381 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm foreign-company status. II. Check annual accounts form, filing and place-of-business list. III. Note any CG notification exceptions.
